clue.text: Fine at avoiding angry passion

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil grades

indicators.note: avoiding says the word at is kept out of the synonym for angry

parts.note: irate means angry

explanation.surface: A cool head ('fine') that steers clear of furious emotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine at' reads like a phrase, but 'at' belongs with 'avoiding': it is the part dropped from the word for angry.
explanation.definitionFit: Fire is a common figurative word for ardour or strong feeling, as in 'the fire of youth'.

clue.text: Runs company investing in excellent plant product

indicators.note: investing in says the pieces are placed inside the word for excellent

parts.note: fine means excellent
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A company running investments in a fine plant product.
explanation.definitionFit: A fir cone is the seed-bearing cone produced by a fir tree.

clue.text: Well-regarded Unionist welcomed by theatre board

indicators.note: welcomed by says the Unionist goes inside the other letters

parts.note: rep is repertory theatre
a table is a board, as in 'board and lodging'

explanation.surface: A respected Unionist politician is welcomed onto a theatre's board.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone reputable has a good reputation, so is well thought of.

clue.text: With friends at sea keeping you finally right as aquatic performer

indicators.note: keeping says the jumbled letters hold another letter inside them
at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters of friends are jumbled
finally picks out the last letter of the word you

explanation.surface: A group of friends out on the water with one, at last, performing correctly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' turns FRIENDS into INDSFER, which keeps U (the end of 'you') to give INDSURFE; W goes in front and R at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A windsurfer rides a sailboard over the water, so is fairly described as someone performing on water.

clue.text: I'd premonition over ENO dropping new Mozart opera

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the earlier pieces stand on top of the next

parts.note: I'd gives ID without the apostrophe
an omen is a premonition

indicators.note: dropping says the N for new is removed from ENO

explanation.surface: A singer has a feeling the English National Opera will drop a new Mozart production.
explanation.walkthrough: ENO is the English National Opera; losing N leaves EO.
explanation.definitionFit: Idomeneo is an opera seria by Mozart, first performed in Munich in 1781.

clue.text: French are gripped by dreadful need

indicators.note: gripped by says the French word is held inside the other

parts.note: dire means dreadful
es is French for (you) are, as in 'tu es'

explanation.surface: The French are in the grip of a terrible need.
explanation.definitionFit: Desire is a strong wish or longing, close to a need for something.

clue.text: Study centre curtailed part of course

indicators.note: curtailed means cut short, so the last letter is removed

parts.note: a unit is one section of an academic course

explanation.surface: A study centre cut back one module of a course.
explanation.definitionFit: Uni is informal British shorthand for university, a place of study.

clue.text: Wintry weather seeing upturn in cloudbursts or fogs

indicators.note: upturn says the hidden letters are read upwards, backwards in this down clue
in says the letters lie inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Signs of cold weather among the rain and mist.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'seeing' as part of the definition; it is only a link word joining 'Wintry weather' to the wordplay. 'in' marks the hidden word, 'upturn' its reading upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Frost is the icy deposit of a freezing night, typical cold-season conditions.

clue.text: Hold back official intelligence after leader's deposed

parts.note: a ref is a referee, a match official

indicators.note: deposed says the leader, the first letter, of the word is removed

parts.note: brain means intelligence

explanation.surface: An official holds back intelligence after a coup topples the leader.
explanation.definitionFit: To refrain is to abstain or stop oneself from doing something.

clue.text: Academic blending coal and schist

indicators.note: blending means mixing together, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A geologist's paper on mixing coal and schist.
explanation.definitionFit: Scholastic relates to schools and learning, matching academic as an adjective.

clue.text: Debts linked to charge account, showing greed

parts.note: a rap is a criminal charge, as in 'beat the rap'
IOUs are written acknowledgements of debts

explanation.surface: Someone running up debts on a charge account, evidently from greed.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue names the debts first, but they come last in the answer: 'linked to' only joins the pieces without fixing their order.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapacious means grasping or avaricious, which is exactly what showing greed describes.

clue.text: India's capital avoided in intermittent part of break

indicators.note: read as 'a void' (an O, a nothing) giving way, with India's letter coming in instead

parts.note: something on-off happens intermittently, stopping and starting

indicators.note: capital here means the capital, or first, letter of the word India

explanation.surface: A cryptic statement that India's capital city was skipped during some stop-start journey.
explanation.walkthrough: Take ON-OFF and replace its first O (the void or nothing) with I. A break in snooker is a run of scoring shots.
explanation.definitionFit: An in-off is a snooker or billiards shot where the ball enters a pocket via another ball, potentially a scoring stroke within a break.

clue.text: University book capturing college result

parts.note: OU is the Open University, Britain's distance-learning university

indicators.note: capturing says the book holds the college letter inside it

parts.note: a tome is a large book

explanation.surface: A university textbook that records the result of a college's work.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcome is the consequence or end result of something.

clue.text: Uproar and cheers after receiving first of cream cheese

indicators.note: after says the thanks come behind the rest
receiving says the uproar takes a letter inside it

parts.note: a riot is an uproar

indicators.note: first of picks the opening letter of cream

parts.note: ta is British slang for thanks, like cheers

explanation.surface: A rowdy crowd cheering after being served cream cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Ricotta is a soft white Italian cheese made from whey.

clue.text: Description of advert not meant for wide distribution?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a small newspaper advertisement
second meaning: secret, as official information restricted to authorised people

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark plays on adverts being meant for wide distribution, while classified documents are not.
explanation.definitionFit: Classified describes both the small sectioned adverts in a paper and officially secret material.

clue.text: Accepted drivers having to enter plant

indicators.note: having to enter says the drivers go inside the plant word

parts.note: to plant something is to embed it
the RAC (Royal Automobile Club) is a British motoring organisation for drivers

explanation.surface: Motorists accepted being forced into a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' looks like a factory or a flower but is the verb meaning to set firmly in place.
explanation.definitionFit: To accept an idea or offer is to embrace it, so accepted and embraced are synonyms.

clue.text: Strike sees one leaving London area

indicators.note: leaving says one's letter departs from the strike word

parts.note: a strike is industrial action
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A walkout in which one worker abandons a London district.
explanation.walkthrough: Acton is a district of west London.
explanation.definitionFit: Acton is a suburb in the London borough of Ealing, so it is a London district.

clue.text: Range's stature is rocky

indicators.note: rocky means unsteady, so the letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone's range of standing is shaky.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Range stands for 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tessitura is the musical term for the pitch span most comfortable for a singer's voice.

clue.text: Perhaps trusty Prince is working with Queen

parts.note: on means working, as in a machine that is on
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A trustworthy prince works alongside the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trusty' looks like an adjective, but a trusty is a trusted inmate given privileges.
explanation.definitionFit: A trusty is a well-behaved jail inmate given privileges, so is an example of one held in custody.

clue.text: To dine beside historic King will be marvellous

indicators.note: beside says the two pieces sit next to each other

parts.note: GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George, seen on old post boxes
to dine is to eat

explanation.surface: Dining next to a king of old would be wonderful.
explanation.definitionFit: Great is an informal word for excellent or wonderful.

clue.text: Very clear endless elegance surrounds this setter

indicators.note: surrounds says the shortened word goes around the setter
endless says the final letter is cut off

parts.note: grace is elegance
Phi is the name of this puzzle's setter

explanation.surface: The setter boasts that boundless elegance surrounds him, very clearly.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often refer to themselves as 'this setter' or 'me'; here it stands for Phi, the compiler's pseudonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Graphic means vividly explicit or detailed, leaving nothing unclear.

clue.text: Man's place is in his area, mostly unsettled

indicators.note: unsettled means disturbed, so the collected letters are rearranged
mostly says the word area loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A man's place lies in his own area, but mostly he is restless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' looks like any man but is the Isle of Man, which lies in the Irish Sea. IS, HIS and ARE are jumbled together.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man sits in the stretch of water between Britain and Ireland, so that sea is where it is located.

clue.text: One gallery featured in film

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards or dice
the Tate is a London art gallery

explanation.surface: A single London gallery appears in a movie.
explanation.definitionFit: Acetate is the plastic film used for overhead transparencies and photographic stock.

clue.text: Children's writer's book I found in home

indicators.note: found in says the letters are placed inside the home word

parts.note: a nest is a home

explanation.surface: A children's author's book turns up at home.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after writer stands for 'has', a link. E. Nesbit wrote The Railway Children.
explanation.definitionFit: Edith Nesbit was the English author of The Railway Children and Five Children and It.

clue.text: Attorney, with some discomfort, representing embassy official

parts.note: Att is the abbreviation for attorney
an ache is a mild, some, discomfort

explanation.surface: A lawyer in mild pain acting for an embassy official.
explanation.definitionFit: An attaché is a diplomat attached to an embassy with a particular specialism.

clue.text: Obligation to include separate bits of toilet, not as a one-off?

indicators.note: to include says the obligation word takes these letters inside it
separate says the two letters of the toilet go in apart, not side by side

parts.note: a tie is an obligation or binding commitment
one of the two bits of WC, water closet, a toilet: its first letter
the other bit of WC, the abbreviation for a toilet: its second letter

explanation.surface: A duty to put bits of a toilet in, and not just once.
explanation.walkthrough: WC (water closet) is split: W goes after the T of TIE and C after the I.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done twice happens on two occasions, so it is not a single isolated event.

clue.text: Be enough to feel bad, mostly, about one with cold

indicators.note: about says the shortened word goes around the other letters
mostly says the last letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: to suffer is to feel bad
I is the Roman numeral for one
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Feeling poorly with a cold, one wonders if it is enough.
explanation.walkthrough: SUFFER without its R is SUFFE, which goes about IC.
explanation.definitionFit: To suffice is to be adequate or sufficient for a purpose.

clue.text: Success capturing American island or part of island

indicators.note: capturing says the success word holds the American letter

parts.note: a hit is a success

explanation.surface: A triumph in securing an American island, or a piece of one.
explanation.walkthrough: Haiti shares the Caribbean island of Hispaniola with the Dominican Republic, so it is only part of an island.
explanation.definitionFit: The nation of Haiti occupies the western third of Hispaniola, the rest being the Dominican Republic.

clue.text: Reserve cereal having mislaid recipe

indicators.note: having mislaid says the recipe letter is lost from the cereal

parts.note: rice is a cereal grain
R is the abbreviation for recipe, from Latin, as on prescriptions

explanation.surface: Keeping cereal in reserve but losing the recipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reserve' looks like a verb but means coolness of manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice can mean coldness or aloofness of manner, the same as reserve in a person.

clue.text: English in lodging house unravelled a clue in Scottish island

indicators.note: in says English goes inside the lodging house

parts.note: a B&B, written BnB, is a bed and breakfast

indicators.note: unravelled means untangled, so the letters of a clue are rearranged

explanation.surface: An English guest at a B&B on a Scottish island cracks a crossword clue.
explanation.walkthrough: E goes into BNB to give BENB; ECULA is a clue rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Benbecula is an island in the Outer Hebrides, off the west coast of Scotland.

clue.text: Church adopting line regarding fiction: a top-level thing for the church

definitions.text: a top-level thing for the church

indicators.note: adopting says the church takes the line letter inside it

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
re means regarding or about
a story is a piece of fiction

explanation.surface: The church taking a line on fiction, with a nod to its upper walls.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is descriptive: a clerestory is the high, windowed part of a church wall, so 'top-level' is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A clerestory is the upper level of a church nave's walls, pierced by windows above the aisle roofs.

clue.text: Dislike not heading for Sahara in expedition

indicators.note: not says the following letter is left out of the speed word

parts.note: expedition can mean speed or promptness, that is haste

indicators.note: heading for picks the first letter of Sahara

explanation.surface: Someone who dislikes not going to the Sahara on a trek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'expedition' looks like a journey, but here it means speed: HASTE loses its S.
explanation.definitionFit: To hate something is to dislike it intensely.
